{{nihongo|'''Ikohayawake-no-Mikoto Shrine'''|伊去波夜和気命神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

=== Enshrined Deities ===
* A total of five deities are enshrined: {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Kami}}, {{ill|Futsunushi|lt=Futsunushi-no-Kami|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286}}, {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}, and {{ill|Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama|Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}} ({{ill|Toyouke-hime|abstract|Q2983724|bcl|Toyoukebime|es|Toyouke Ōmikami|fr|Toyouke Ōmikami|ja|トヨウケビメ|kk|Тоёукэ бимэ|ru|Тоёукэ бимэ|simple|Toyōke Ōmikami|sv|Toyouke Ōmikami|tok|jan sewi suli Tojoke|zh|豐宇氣毘賣神|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyouke Ōkami}}).  
It is said that the collective name of these deities is '''“Ikohayawake-no-Mikoto.”'''

=== History ===
The date of the shrine’s founding is unknown. Originally, the shrine buildings were located elsewhere, but they were transferred to the present Watanoha Ōmiya location in the 8th year of {{ill|Kansei|arz|كانسى|de|Kansei|fa|کانسی (دوره)|fr|Ère Kansei|id|Kansei|ja|寛政|ko|간세이|pt|Era Kansei|ru|Кансэй|simple|Kansei|sr|Кансеи|sv|Kansei|tr|Kansei|zh|寬政|qid=Q1195131}}.  
Among the 100 {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} in Mutsu Province listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, this shrine is known by the names “Hama Daimyōjin” and “Shiromori Myōjin.” Today it is commonly called “Myōjinsha” and is worshipped as a deity of abundant fishing, maritime safety, and salt production.

Among the enshrined deities, Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto (considered identical to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiotsuchi-no-Oji-no-Kami}}), Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto, and Futsunushi-no-Mikoto are also deities of {{ill|Shiogama shrine|abstract|Q133753|fr|Shiogama-jinja|ja|鹽竈神社|ru|Сиогама-дзиндзя|simple|Shiogama Shrine|zh|鹽竈神社|qid=Q133753}}, the Ichinomiya of Ōshū. Amaterasu Ōmikami and Ukanomitama-no-Kami (Toyouke Ōkami) are the deities of the Inner and Outer Shrines of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}.

On March 11, 2011, the tsunami caused by the {{ill|2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|af|Tōhoku-aardbewing en -tsoenami van 2011|als|Tōhoku-Erdbeben 2011|ar|زلزال وتسونامي توهوكو 2011|arz|زلزال و تسونامى سينداى|ast|Terremotu y tsunami de Xapón de 2011|az|Tohoku zəlzələsi və sunamisi (2011)|bat_smg|2011 metu Sendajė žemės kostiejėms ė cunamis|bcl|Linog asin Dolnop sa Tōhoku (2011)|be|Землетрасенне ў Японіі (2011)|be_x_old|Землятрус у Японіі (2011)|bg|Земетресение в регион Тохоку (2011)|bjn|Lindu wan tsunami Sendai 2011|bn|২০১১ টোহুকু ভূমিকম্প ও সুনামি|bs|Zemljotres i cunami u Tōhokuu 2011.|ca|Terratrèmol i tsunami del Japó del 2011|ckb|بوومەلەرزە و تسۆنامی ٢٠١١ی تۆھۆکۆ|cs|Zemětřesení a tsunami v Tóhoku (2011)|cu|Ꙁємлѥтрѩсѥниѥ Ꙗпѡнїи 2011 лѣта|cy|Daeargryn a tsunami Sendai 2011|da|Jordskælvet ved Sendai 2011|de|Tōhoku-Erdbeben 2011|el|Σεισμός και τσουνάμι στο Τόχοκου το 2011|eo|Tertremo de Tōhoku en 2011|es|Terremoto y tsunami de Japón de 2011|et|2011. aasta Sendai maavärin|eu|2011ko Sendaiko lurrikara eta tsunamia|fa|زمین‌لرزه و سونامی ۲۰۱۱ توهوکو|fi|Tōhokun maanjäristys ja tsunami|fo|Jarðskjálvtin í Sendai 2011|fr|Séisme de 2011 de la côte Pacifique du Tōhoku|ga|Crith talún Tohoku agus súnámaí, 2011|gl|Terremoto e tsunami de Sendai de 2011|gv|Craa thallooin as tsunami Tōhoku, 2011|he|רעידת האדמה והצונאמי בטוהוקו (2011)|hi|२०११ सेन्दाई भूकम्प और सुनामी|hr|Potres i cunami u Sendaiju 2011.|hu|2011-es tóhokui földrengés és cunami|hy|Երկրաշարժ Ճապոնիայում (2011)|id|Gempa bumi dan tsunami Tōhoku 2011|is|Hamfarirnar í Japan 2011|it|Terremoto e maremoto del Tōhoku del 2011|ja|東北地方太平洋沖地震|jv|Lindhu lan tsunami Sendai 2011|ka|ტოჰოკუს მიწისძვრა და ცუნამი (2011)|kk|Жапониядағы жер сілкінісі (2011)|ko|도호쿠 지방 태평양 해역 지진|ksh|Sendai-Ärdbebe va 2011|la|Terrae motus Tohoku|lt|2011 m. The subsidiary shrines, shrine office, and the chief priest’s residence were damaged; however, people who evacuated to the shrine’s haiden, which stands slightly elevated and surrounded by a sacred forest, were unharmed.

Since then, thanks to the efforts of volunteers and parishioners, recovery has progressed with the shrine at the center of the community’s collective efforts.

* Within the approach and precincts are an ema hall, a sumo ring for dedication matches, stone shrines, and other features.

=== Enshrined Deity ===
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiotsuchi-no-Oji-no-Mikoto}}

=== History ===
Both the founding and history of this shrine are unknown. One theory holds that it was founded in the 15th year of the {{ill|Hakuhō|Q11580612|qid=Q11580612}} era, and it is regarded as a candidate shrine for the Shikinaisha Ikohayawake-no-Mikoto Shrine.
